For him the Father, God, hath {{ls}}igned. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=28}} They {{ls}}aid therfore vnto him, VVhat {{ls}}hal vve doe that vve may vvorke the vvorkes of God? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=29}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered, and {{ls}}aid to them, This is the vvorke of God, that you beleeue in him vvhom he hath {{ls}}ent. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=30}} They {{ls}}aid therfore to him, VVhat {{ls}}igne therfore doe{{ls}}t thou, that vve may {{ls}}ee, and may beleeue thee? vvhat vvorke{{ls}}t thou?

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=31}} Our {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 16, 4. 14. P{{ls}}. 77, 24.''}}* fathers did eate Manna in the de{{ls}}ert, as it is vvritten, ''Bread from heauen he gaue them to eate''. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=32}} {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore {{ls}}aid to them, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ why we keepe the hebrue word, ''Amen'', & tran{{ls}}late it not, See the Annot. ''c. 8. ver{{ls}}. 34''.}}∷ Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you, Moy{{ls}}es gaue you not the bread from heauen, but my Father giueth you {{sup|‖}} the true bread from heauen. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=33}} For the bread of God it is that de{{ls}}cendeth from heauen, and giueth life to the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=34}} They {{ls}}aid therfore vnto him, Lord, giue vs alvvaies this bread. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=35}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid to them, I am the bread of life, he that commeth to me, {{ls}}hal not hunger: and he that beleeueth in me, {{ls}}hal neuer thir{{ls}}t. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=36}} But I {{ls}}aid to you that both you haue {{ls}}een me and you beleeue not. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=37}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Go{{ls}}pel in the Anniuer{{ls}}arie of the dead.}}∷ Al that the Father giueth me, {{ls}}hal come to me: and him that commeth to me I vvil not ca{{ls}}t forth. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=38}} Becau{{ls}}e I de{{ls}}cended from heauen, not to doe mine ovvne vvil, but the vvil of him that {{ls}}ent me. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=39}} For this is the vvil of him that {{ls}}ent me, the Father: that al that he hath giuen me I lee{{ls}}e not thereof, but rai{{ls}}e it in the la{{ls}}t day. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=40}} And this is the vvil of my father that {{ls}}ent me: that euery one that {{ls}}eeth the Sonne, and beleeueth in him, haue life euerla{{ls}}ting, and I vvil rai{{ls}}e him in the la{{ls}}t day.⊣

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=41}} The Ievves therfore murmured at him, becau{{ls}}e he had {{ls}}aid, I am the bread vvhich de{{ls}}cended from heauen: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=42}} and they {{ls}}aid, Is not this {{sc|Iesvs}} the {{ls}}onne of Io{{ls}}eph, vvho{{ls}}e father and mother vve knovv? Hovv then {{ls}}aith he, That I de{{ls}}cended from heauen? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=43}} {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore an{{ls}}vvered and {{ls}}aid to them, Murmure not one to an other: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=44}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō Imber vvene{{ls}}day in vvhit{{ls}}onvveeke,}}no man can come to me, vnles the Father that {{ls}}ent me, {{sup|‖}} dravv him: and I vvil rai{{ls}}e him vp in the la{{ls}}t day. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=45}} It is vvritten in the Prophets, ''And al {{ls}}hal be docible of God''. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''E{{ls}}a. 54, 13.''}}* Euery one that hath heard of the Father, and hath learned, commeth to me. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=46}} Not that any man hath {{ls}}een the Father, but he vvhich is of God: this hath {{ls}}een the Father. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=47}} Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you, he that beleeueth in me, hath life euerla{{ls}}ting. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=48}} I am the bread of life. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=49}} Your fathers did eate {{sup|‖}} Manna in the de{{ls}}ert: and they died.<noinclude>{{rh|||This}}</noinclude>
